writeup.headline: UnitedHealth rates Hold: a raised outlook and firm trend offset slowing growth and thin operating margins.
writeup.thesis: UnitedHealth scores 58, a Hold, with no factor strong or weak enough to tip it either way. Valuation (69) is the strongest support: in absolute terms the shares look low at 0.8x sales, 15.5x free cash flow and 18.8x EV/EBIT, with an FCF yield 1.5 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield, though against its own history it sits near the middle of its own history (the multiples disagree: P/S cheap, P/FCF cheap, EV/EBIT expensive). The price trend (65) is also helpful, with the price 12.4% above its 200-day average and shares 2.0 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. Growth (36) is the main drag: TTM revenue growth of 6.5% hides latest-quarter revenue growth of only 0.4% year on year, and growth slowed by 1.6 pp from the previous quarter. Quality (64) and balance sheet (62) are middling, with an operating margin of 4.8% and an FCF margin of 5.2%, while news (58) balances a Q3 beat and raised FY2026 outlook against new litigation.
key_risks: Revenue growth is stalling, with latest-quarter growth of just 0.4% year on year and slowing momentum.
Thin operating margin of 4.8% leaves little room if medical costs rise.
Litigation, including the partly surviving CalPERS securities suit and employer suits over alleged overpaid claims.
Medicare Advantage plan cuts covering about 390,000 members and falling Optum Health revenue.
Net debt at 1.77x free cash flow and cash covering only 0.43x debt, with the company still working toward its debt-to-capital target.
what_would_change: A move to Buy needs 7 more points, most plausibly from growth re-accelerating from its 36 score.
Delivering on the raised FY2026 outlook and improving margins could lift quality and news scores.
A drop to Sell would require losing 14 points, such as a reversal in price trend combined with weaker news or guidance.
Adverse litigation outcomes or regulatory action could pull the news risk score down.
